verdict: Loews earned $306M, down from $504M a year ago, as a $125M long-term care reserve charge at insurer CNA and weaker underwriting outweighed solid growth at Boardwalk Pipelines and Loews Hotels.

kpis.note: total revenue vs a year ago

kpis.label: Net income
kpis.note: attributable to Loews, vs $504M a year ago

segments.name: CNA Financial (insurance)
segments.note: The insurer CNA — about 80% of Loews. Premiums, investment income and other insurance revenue; flat vs a year ago as a long-term care reserve charge hit earnings, not revenue.

segments.name: Boardwalk Pipelines
segments.note: Natural gas pipelines and storage — revenue up 13% on higher gas transportation rates and utilization.

segments.name: Loews Hotels & Co
segments.note: Hotels — revenue up 18% on higher room rates and more occupied nights, led by the renovated Loews Miami Beach Hotel.

segments.name: Corporate investment income
segments.note: Investment income earned by the parent company itself, down from $97M a year ago.

opex.name: Operating expenses & other
opex.note: Everything else Loews spends — running the pipelines, hotels and insurance operations, plus corporate costs — in Loews' own reported line.

otherDetail: There is no separate other-income line in Loews' presentation: $406M is income before tax. The $16M shown here is the share of profit attributable to noncontrolling interests, deducted so the bottom line is the $306M attributable to Loews shareholders.

takeaways.title: A reserve charge hit CNA
takeaways.text: CNA's annual long-term care reserve review produced an unfavorable $125M impact (after tax and noncontrolling interests). CNA's core income fell to $203M from $409M, and the P&C combined ratio rose to 97.0% from 92.8% on higher catastrophe losses and loss-cost trends. Loews notes the charge should be almost entirely offset over time by higher investment yields.

takeaways.title: Boardwalk kept growing
takeaways.text: Pipeline revenue rose 13% to $616M on higher gas transportation rates and utilization. Net income of $85M included about $14M (after tax) of one-off charges — unrealized losses at Continuum and an office-relocation impairment; excluding them, results improved.

takeaways.title: Buybacks continue
takeaways.text: Loews repurchased 1.6 million of its own shares for $167M in the quarter and held $4.4B of cash and investments at the parent. Book value per share excluding AOCI rose to $100.67, from $95.89 at the end of 2025.

oneTimers: CNA's annual long-term care reserve assumption update: an unfavorable $125M impact on Loews' share of CNA's earnings (after tax and noncontrolling interests) — the single biggest reason profit fell year over year.
Boardwalk took about $14M (after tax) of charges: $7M of net unrealized losses at Continuum and a $7M impairment tied to relocating its corporate office.
footerNote: Loews is a holding company, so this page follows its own presentation (like the bank and insurer pages): revenue is shown by business as Loews reports it — CNA insurance, Boardwalk Pipelines, Loews Hotels & Co and parent-company investment income. By type, revenue was insurance premiums $2,829M, net investment income $713M, investment losses of $9M and operating revenues and other $1,226M. Insurance claims and policyholders' benefits ($2,347M) play the role of cost of revenue. Net income is the $306M attributable to Loews; consolidated net income was $322M.
